overall_summary: Overall view counts are very low across the board (ranging from 5 to 40 views), meaning statistical confidence is quite low. However, 'self respect' and personal digital boundary topics (like clearing chats and removing numbers) tend to perform relatively better compared to generic emotional topics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on self-respect actions like deleting chats or removing saved numbers (e.g., 'चैट डिलीट करने की हिम्मत', 'बिना नाम के नंबर') gained relative peaks up to 40 views.
winning_patterns.action: Focus storytelling on micro-actions related to phone screens, chats, and setting personal boundaries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Broad night-time or tea-drinking tropes (e.g., 'रात के दो बजे', 'चाय ठंडी हो गई') underperformed significantly, hitting lows of 5-12 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague ambient setups; tie emotional moments to specific, tangible everyday digital triggers.

next_video.concept: Turning off read receipts so they can no longer see when you've seen their message, reclaiming your peace.
next_video.opening_direction: Blue ticks turned off for just one specific contact.
next_video.twist_direction: Realizing the freedom that comes when they can no longer check if you're waiting.
next_video.reason: Tests if practical digital self-respect actions can sustain the relative success seen in previous boundary-setting shorts.

experiment: Testing if specific notification privacy settings ('last seen' or 'read receipts') drive higher engagement than broader chat deletion concepts.
